task_completion.description: Open the Export Log menu in Subsurface
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Export' dialog window or menu is visible over the main Subsurface interface.

task_completion.description: Select the HTML export tab or format option
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'HTML' tab is selected or highlighted within the Export dialog.

task_completion.description: Ensure 'All dives' option is selected for export
task_completion.visual_evidence: A radio button or checkbox labeled 'All dives' or 'Export all dives' is selected in the export settings.
The file save dialog or the path input field shows '/home/ga/Documents/WebLog/divelog.html' or '~/Documents/WebLog/divelog.html'.
The 'Export' or 'Save' button is clicked, or a progress bar for the export appears.

task_completion.description: Verify the exported file exists in the file manager or browser
task_completion.visual_evidence: A file manager (like Nautilus) shows 'divelog.html' in the 'WebLog' folder, or a web browser displays the exported logbook with dive data.

integrity.description: The agent used the Subsurface GUI to perform the export rather than just creating a file via terminal
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show interactions with the Subsurface 'File' menu and 'Export' dialog boxes.

integrity.description: The agent did not use 'touch' or 'echo' in a terminal to fake the output file
integrity.visual_evidence: The terminal history (if visible) does not show commands creating the divelog.html file manually.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the specific Subsurface application window
integrity.visual_evidence: The Subsurface application icon and window title are visible during the export process.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The expected export path is /home/ga/Documents/WebLog/divelog.html. The source data contains dives from 'Sund Rock'. A successful export will result in an HTML file significantly larger than 10KB because it bundles CSS/JS and dive data.
